version_finding.explanation: pgmnemo 0.18.0 silently defaulted _graph_weight=0.0 due to unregistered GUC (EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS catch). ARM_B in first pilot was equivalent to ARM_A — no BFS ran. pgmnemo 0.18.1 fixed GUC registration; BFS now runs with _max_depth=5, causing catastrophic expansion on hub nodes (temporal out_degree ~200+). D3 repair (max_depth 5→2) is required before a valid quality ablation can be run.

cycle_protection_check.note: D1 cycle guard (visited BIGINT[]) IS present in installed 0.18.1 function. D3 (max_depth 5→2) is NOT applied. Without D3, depth=5 BFS on hub nodes (temporal out_degree 176–220) produces polynomial node expansion causing timeouts.

primary_quality_test.note: ARM_A baseline recall@10=0.0 on graph-sensitive probes (cosine<0.7). Probe construction selects pairs too semantically distant for targets to appear in HNSW+BM25 candidate set. Graph boost as a re-ranker (not expander) cannot promote targets not in the candidate pool. This is an additional secondary finding independent of the latency issue.

section_7_verdict.conclusion: ARM_B timeout rate 96.0% ≥ 5% (§7 threshold). Graph walk at δ=0.2, max_depth=5 is unsafe to enable on this 74,778-edge corpus with hub nodes having temporal out_degree 176–220. §7 finding: graph is unsafe to enable — publish as latency-safety result separate from quality finding. D3 repair (max_depth 5→2) required before quality ablation can be completed.

subgroup_analysis.note: All pilot probes are temporal edges (causal/temporal pool, temporal=97% of eligible)

required_next_steps: Apply D3 repair: set max_depth=2 in installed recall_hybrid (pgmnemo--0.18.0--0.19.0.sql §3)
Verify ARM_B latency returns to <200ms with no timeouts at n=10 warmup probes
Re-run full ablation per ABLATION_PROTOCOL_88 v1 Amendment A (n=1500)
Note: ARM_A recall@10=0.0 finding may also need probe redesign (current cosine<0.7 filter too strict for this corpus's HNSW candidate pool)
